verdict.line: You lose if Mordekaiser gets you into a sustained melee trade where his passive and shield take over; you win by poking from range and never giving him that fight.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser has nothing that out-ranges Jayce's Cannon-stance Shock Blast except Obliterate's 675-range smash, so the lane is decided by whether Jayce lets him close the gap. His real power comes from Darkness Rise triggering a damage aura after 3 hits land and from Indestructible banking damage into a heal — both only matter in prolonged melee exchanges. The 47.9% win rate over 215 games and Mordekaiser's solo-kill edge both come from Jayce players getting pulled into those extended fights instead of poking and resetting.

theirWindow.when: after he pulls you with E
theirWindow.what: Death's Grasp drags you into melee range where his passive aura and W (Indestructible) banked shield take over the fight. Don't trade autos here — disengage immediately.

yourWindow.when: you're at max range with Q up
yourWindow.what: Poke with Shock Blast (Q, Cannon stance) and autos from outside his 675-range Obliterate. He has no way to close distance except Death's Grasp, which is on a long cooldown early.

start.why: 49.8% win rate over 259 games and the dominant pick (94.5%) — the extra sustain matters because every trade you take should be a poke, not a brawl, and the potion buys time to reset.

boots.why: 48.6% win rate over 107 games. Cooldown reduction tightens the Cannon-stance Q poke / R stance-swap loop so you can keep resetting his passive stacks without losing tempo.

core.why: Builds toward Muramana's mana-spend poke damage, which is how you punish him from range instead of in melee where he wants you.
Active haste lets you disengage the instant he lands Death's Grasp or closes distance, denying the extended fight he needs.
Converts your mana pool into the burst poke damage that defines this matchup — hit and leave before his passive triggers.

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards exactly the pattern this matchup demands — hit him, gain move speed, leave before his passive or Death's Grasp catches you in melee.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport runs a 55.9% win rate over this matchup, well above Flash+Ignite's 44.8% — Teleport lets you play the lane safely for the poke-and-scale plan instead of forcing an early kill you don't need.

playing.title: Poke, don't duel
playing.detail: Stay in Cannon stance and fire Shock Blast (Q) and autos from max range. Never stand in melee trading — that's the only way his passive aura and W shield come online.

playing.title: Track his hit count on you
playing.detail: Darkness Rise activates after 3 landed hits and grants him a damage aura plus move speed. If he's landed two, back off before the third connects.

playing.title: Respect Death's Grasp's cooldown
playing.detail: E is 16/14/12/10/8s on a 700 range. Early, once he's used it to pull you, you have a long window where he has no way to close distance again — use it to reset the poke.

playing.title: Swap to Hammer to punish dives
playing.detail: If he does close distance, flip R into Hammer stance and use Thundering Blow (E) to knock him back and reset spacing instead of trading autos in melee.

playing.title: Never facetank Obliterate
playing.detail: Q hits hardest on a single target at 675 range — don't stand still and let him land it for free; it's his only tool that out-ranges your Cannon-stance Q.

playing.title: Buy Serpent's Fang once he's stacking Indestructible
playing.detail: His W banks damage dealt and taken into a heal. If fights are stalling because of it, shredding that shield turns your poke damage back into real pressure.

playing.title: Play for scaling, not pre-6 all-ins
playing.detail: Solo-kill advantage is his. Farm safely off Cannon-stance poke through level 5-6 and let Muramana and item spikes win the mid-game instead of forcing a trade you don't need.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own read of the ability kits.

stats.opponentTip: Keep some distance to deactivate Mordekaiser’s (P). Rather than fighting in prolonged combat, try to poke him instead.
